paper.note: Page ground. Printed with a two-axis repeating-gradient fibre tooth at ~2% ink opacity so it reads as stock, not as flat grey.

ink.note: All primary text, the masthead bar, heavy rules, reversed-type marks. Warm — never #000.

rule.note: The default 1px rule and the colour a gap-px grid gutter shows through.

scarlet.note: Default section ink, and the fixed danger/alarm role in every section.

scarlet-text.note: The on-newsprint legible variant used for destructive labels and links.

cobalt.note: Pinned section for every /admin route and the profile form. Its -text variant is the same value.

jade.note: Order history, the receipt header flood, the grand total, and the ok flash.

chrome.note: The one light ink: reverses to soft black rather than white.

chrome-text.note: Heavily darkened; the raw amber is unreadable on newsprint.

section-on.note: Foreground on a flooded section ink. Resolves to soft black under chrome.

masthead.purpose: The KABSHOP nameplate on the front page only — and that page's h1.

h1.purpose: Route titles at sm and up; product names on wide screens.

h2.purpose: Default RunningHead title, auth-frame headings, receipt confirmation.

h3.purpose: The rack's live section name; the checkout grand total.

h4.purpose: Product cell price, back-office section headings, order serial.

base.purpose: Product descriptions and input text; prose capped at 68ch.

small.purpose: The workhorse: cell titles, rows, metadata, button labels.

caption.purpose: Notes under figures, breadcrumbs, helper text.

label.purpose: Uppercase Kanit eyebrow for field labels, dt terms, section flags.

figure.purpose: Every number in the product — price, stock, quantity, phone, serial — in tabular lining Kanit.

shadows.name: pressure-section
shadows.purpose: Hover on a filled section-ink or scarlet control. Pressure, not elevation.

shadows.name: pressure-ink
shadows.purpose: Hover on a filled soft-black control — the same gesture reversed out.

shadows.name: spine
shadows.purpose: Structural, not stateful: the vertical registration rule down every Sheet.

motion.name: ease-press
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Fast out, long settle — a stamp landing.

motion.name: rule-draw
motion.value: scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1) over 520ms ease-press, transform-origin left
motion.purpose: Rules draw themselves left to right. Used by PageLoading's three staggered bars (0/90/180ms).

motion.name: ink-settle
motion.purpose: Product cells arriving in the rack, staggered 26ms per cell and capped at 12 cells.

motion.name: flash-in
motion.purpose: Flash messages dropping in from the top edge; also the index drawer.

motion.name: state-150
motion.purpose: Default duration for colour, border and box-shadow state changes on controls.

motion.name: section-300
motion.purpose: Flash rules re-inking when the live section changes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> all animation and transition durations forced to 0.01ms
motion.purpose: Global honour of the OS setting.

narrative.overview:
KABSHOP is set as the classified section of a Thai daily. A general store that carries everything has no single vertical to dress itself in, so it borrows the one layout built for exactly that problem: a ruled sheet where anything can be listed next to anything, and the reader still knows where they are. Rules are the material. Not decoration between things — the thing itself. Cells sit shoulder to shoulder separated by a single hairline; grids draw their gutters by letting a rule-coloured parent show through one-pixel gaps. Where a marketplace would float a rounded card on grey, this sheet prints a white block on newsprint and draws a line around it.

The ground is real stock. Newsprint (#edebe4) carries a two-axis repeating-gradient fibre tooth so it reads as a sheet rather than as a flat grey; cells are printed on cell stock (#fbfaf7), a lighter, cleaner white. Depth comes from that stock difference and from rule weight — hairline, 3px, 6px, border-t-2 — never from a shadow. Four flat section inks (scarlet, cobalt, jade, chrome) flood whole regions rather than tinting small ones, and only one is live at a time: it is set as a data attribute on the document root, so choosing a category re-rules the masthead flash, the index, the section head, the focus ring, the caret, the text selection and every cell shoulder in a single move.

Money is the headline. Every baht, stock count, quantity, phone number and order serial in the product is set in one numeral treatment — Kanit, tabular lining figures — on the rack, in the cart, at checkout and on the receipt alike. The price is the largest type inside a product cell, larger than the product's own name, because the trust moment in a general store is the number. Interface language is Thai throughout; Kanit and Sarabun are both loaded with the Thai subset, and the type ramp's line-heights are set generous enough for Thai ascenders and tone marks.
keyCharacteristics: Newsprint ground with a printed fibre tooth; white cell stock on top of it.
Hairline rules as the structural material — including as grid gutters (gap-px).
Four flat section inks, one live at a time, set on the document root.
Zero border radius and zero drop shadows anywhere in the build.
One numeral treatment for every figure, storefront through receipt.
Reversed-type blocks for state; no pastel tint chips.
Thai-first typography: Kanit for display and figures, Sarabun for text.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Exactly one section ink is live per page, set as document.documentElement.dataset.section and cleared on unmount. Never hardcode a second ink into a region to "add colour" — if a surface needs an ink, it reads the live one via var(--section-fill). The only inks allowed outside the live section are scarlet as the danger/alarm role and jade as the success role.

rules.name: The Flood Rule
rules.body: Section ink arrives as a solid flood of a whole region — a full-bleed flash rule, a filled index cell, a filled receipt header — or as a 3px–6px bar. It is never a 10% tint behind text and never a border-only accent on an otherwise neutral block.

rules.name: The Reversed-Type Rule
rules.body: State is printed, not tinted. Stock warnings, flash messages and status marks are solid ink blocks with reversed type; there are no pale pastel chips anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The One Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every figure a reader might check — price, subtotal, shipping, grand total, stock count, cart count, quantity, phone number, order serial, accumulated spend — is set with .u-fig. Same face, same tabular lining figures, same tracking, on the storefront, in the drawer, at checkout and on the printed receipt. Never let a number inherit Sarabun.

rules.name: The Price-Is-The-Headline Rule
rules.body: Inside a product cell the price is the largest type in the block (h4, above a 14px title); on the product page it is set at 40px in the section text ink, above everything but the product name. If a layout makes the price smaller than its neighbours, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The Single Nameplate Rule
rules.body: Every route carries exactly one <h1>. On the storefront it is the masthead wordmark itself (Masthead size="full" renders the wordmark as h1); every other route renders size="strip", where the wordmark drops to a span and the page's own RunningHead (default as="h1") supplies the heading.

rules.name: The Spine Rule
rules.body: Content inside a Sheet never sits flush left. It registers to the spine's hairline with a 16/24px indent, the way columns register to a margin rule.

rules.name: The Hairline Gutter Rule
rules.body: A grid of cells separates its cells with gap-px over a bg-rule parent. Do not add per-cell borders that would double up into 2px seams, and do not use empty space where a rule belongs.

rules.name: The Pressure-Not-Lift Rule
rules.body: A control under the cursor gets an inset bottom bar and, on :active, translate-y-px. It never lifts, never gains an offset block shadow, and never scales. The one scale in the system is a 1.03 image zoom inside a product cell's fixed frame, which reads as the picture moving under the crop, not the cell rising.

rules.name: The Section-On-Root Rule
rules.body: A page that belongs to a section sets document.documentElement.dataset.section in an effect and deletes it on cleanup. The back office and the profile form pin cobalt; order history pins jade; the storefront and product pages hash their category name through inkFor() to one of the four. Nothing else should set section colour, and no component should accept an ink as a prop.

dos: Do draw structure with rules at four weights — 1px rule, 3px, 6px, border-2 border-ink — and let the heaviest one frame the most important block on the page.
Do build grids as grid gap-px bg-rule with bg-stock children so the gutter is the hairline.
Do set every number with .u-fig, including phone numbers, counts and order serials.
Do read the live ink through var(--section-fill) / var(--section-text) / var(--section-on); set the section once, on the document root, and clean it up on unmount.
Do print state as a word plus a solid block — "ไม่สำเร็จ", "เหลือ 2 ชิ้น" — so colour is never the only carrier of meaning.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px or more (min-h-[46px] is the house default) and keep the section-ink :focus-visible outline visible.
Do cap running prose at 68ch with u-measure.
Do use Sheet for page width so content registers to the spine.
Do write interface copy in Thai and format numbers, dates and currency with th-TH locale formatting.
donts: Don't add a border radius to anything. Not a card, not a button, not an avatar, not a badge. The zero-radius rule has no exceptions in the shipped build.
Don't add a drop shadow, a lift, an offset block shadow or a glow. Hover pressure is an inset bottom bar; that is the entire elevation vocabulary.
Don't tint. No 10%-opacity ink washes behind text, no pastel status chips — a section ink either floods a region or draws a bar.
Don't put two section inks on one page. Scarlet-as-danger and jade-as-success are the only inks that may appear beside the live one.
Don't hardcode an ink hex in a component (a chart dataset, an inline style) when var(--cobalt) or var(--section-fill) is available — a hardcoded hex will not re-rule when the section changes.
Don't let a product's title outweigh its price, or set money in Sarabun.
Don't render a second <h1> on a route; on the storefront the masthead nameplate is already it, so inner pages must use Masthead size="strip".
Don't introduce a third typeface, a system display face, or an icon font. Kanit, Sarabun and Lucide line icons are the whole kit.
Don't drop input font-size below 16px, or remove the 2px baseline that makes a field read as a compositor's slug.
Don't call window.alert(); push a flash.
